intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) can be caused by heterozygous mutation in the SCN5A gene (600163) on chromosome 3p22, occurring together with variants in the connexin-40 gene GJA5 (121013) on chromosome 1q21, consistent with digenic inheritance.

checks.claim: Atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) can be caused by heterozygous mutation in the SCN5A gene occurring together with variants in the connexin-40 gene GJA5, consistent with digenic inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: In this study, familial AS was associated with the concurrence of a cardiac sodium channel mutation and rare polymorphisms in the atrial-specific Cx40 gene.
checks.explanation: Abstract supports concurrence of SCN5A mutation and Cx40 polymorphisms, but heterozygosity is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The SCN5A gene is located on chromosome 3p22.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A (D1275N)
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene named in the paper.

checks.claim: The connexin-40 gene GJA5 is located on chromosome 1q21.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene for the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin40 (Cx40)
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene named in the paper.

paragraphs.text: Atrial standstill is a rare arrhythmia in which the atria show no electrical or mechanical activity. On the electrocardiogram there are no P waves, and the rhythm is a slow junctional escape rhythm. Atrial stimulation cannot capture the atria. The condition can lead to thromboembolism and usually needs pacemaker implantation. In familial cases, the disorder has been linked to mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A occurring together with variants in the atrial gap junction gene GJA5 (connexin-40).

checks.claim: Atrial standstill is a rare arrhythmia in which the atria show no electrical or mechanical activity.
checks.evidence_quote: Atrial standstill (AS) is a rare arrhythmia that occasionally appears to be genetically determined.
checks.explanation: Abstract states it is a rare arrhythmia but does not describe absence of electrical/mechanical activity.

paragraphs.text: Groenewegen et al. (2003) studied a family with familial atrial standstill. Affected members had no P waves, bradycardia with junctional escape rhythm, and atria that did not respond to electrical stimulation.

checks.claim: Groenewegen et al. (2003) studied a family with familial atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: This study investigates the genetic background of this arrhythmogenic disorder in a large family.

checks.claim: Affected members of the familial atrial standstill family studied by Groenewegen et al. (2003) had no P waves.
checks.explanation: Clinical ECG details (no P waves) are not in the abstract; may be in full text.

checks.claim: Affected members of the familial atrial standstill family studied by Groenewegen et al. (2003) had bradycardia with junctional escape rhythm.
checks.explanation: Bradycardia/junctional escape rhythm not described in the abstract.

checks.claim: In affected members of the familial atrial standstill family studied by Groenewegen et al. (2003), the atria did not respond to electrical stimulation.
checks.explanation: Lack of atrial response to stimulation not described in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Makita et al. (2005) described a Japanese family with congenital atrial standstill.

checks.claim: Makita et al. (2005) described a Japanese family with congenital atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: The purpose of this study was to determine the clinical and biophysical characteristics of a novel SCN5A mutation identified in a family with atrial standstill.
checks.explanation: The family with atrial standstill is described, but the abstract does not state that it is Japanese.

paragraphs.text: The findings of Groenewegen et al. (2003) suggested digenic inheritance of familial atrial standstill. Affected members carried both an SCN5A mutation and a rare GJA5 (connexin-40) genotype, whereas family members with the SCN5A mutation alone were unaffected.

checks.claim: The findings of Groenewegen et al. (2003) suggested digenic inheritance of familial atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: We propose that, although the functional effect of each genetic change is relatively benign, the combined effect of genetic changes eventually progresses to total AS.

checks.claim: In the atrial standstill family studied by Groenewegen et al. (2003), affected members carried both an SCN5A mutation and a rare GJA5 (connexin-40) genotype.
checks.evidence_quote: The three living AS patients exclusively coinherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the SCN5A-D1275N mutation.

checks.claim: In the atrial standstill family studied by Groenewegen et al. (2003), family members carrying the SCN5A mutation alone were unaffected.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed a novel mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A (D1275N) in all three affected living relatives and in five unaffected relatives
checks.explanation: Five unaffected relatives carried the mutation; only affected patients coinherited both changes.

paragraphs.text: Atrial standstill is genetically heterogeneous. An autosomal recessive form, atrial standstill-2 (ATRST2), is caused by mutation in the NPPA gene.

checks.claim: Atrial standstill is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. Genetic heterogeneity is not addressed in the abstract.

checks.claim: Atrial standstill-2 (ATRST2) is an autosomal recessive form of atrial standstill caused by mutation in the NPPA gene.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. NPPA and ATRST2 are not mentioned.

paragraphs.text: In a family with atrial standstill, Groenewegen et al. (2003) identified a heterozygous asp1275-to-asn (D1275N) mutation in the SCN5A gene. The mutation segregated with the disease together with a rare genotype of 2 linked polymorphisms in the regulatory region of the connexin-40 gene (GJA5). The authors proposed that the combination of reduced sodium channel function and altered connexin-40 expression caused the loss of atrial excitability. In their functional studies, the D1275N channel showed only modest changes in gating properties.

checks.claim: Groenewegen et al. (2003) identified a heterozygous asp1275-to-asn (D1275N) mutation in the SCN5A gene in a family with atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: Candidate gene screening revealed a novel mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A (D1275N) in all three affected living relatives
checks.explanation: Mutation confirmed; heterozygosity not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the atrial standstill family studied by Groenewegen et al. (2003), the SCN5A D1275N mutation segregated with the disease together with a rare genotype of 2 linked polymorphisms in the regulatory region of the connexin-40 gene (GJA5).
checks.evidence_quote: two closely linked polymorphisms were detected within regulatory regions of the gene for the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin40 (Cx40) at nucleotides -44 (G-->A) and +71 (A-->G).
checks.explanation: Together with exclusive coinheritance in affected patients.

checks.claim: Groenewegen et al. (2003) proposed that the combination of reduced sodium channel function and altered connexin-40 expression caused the loss of atrial excitability in atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: We propose that, although the functional effect of each genetic change is relatively benign, the combined effect of genetic changes eventually progresses to total AS.
checks.explanation: Combined effect proposed; 'reduced sodium channel function' and 'loss of atrial excitability' phrasing is not explicit in abstract (channel showed depolarizing shift; Cx40 reporter expression reduced).

checks.claim: In functional studies by Groenewegen et al. (2003), the SCN5A D1275N channel showed only modest changes in gating properties.
checks.evidence_quote: SCN5A-D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation compared with wild-type channels.

paragraphs.text: In a Japanese family with congenital atrial standstill, Makita et al. (2005) found a novel SCN5A mutation that was inherited together with connexin-40 polymorphisms. This supported the model of SCN5A and GJA5 coinheritance proposed by Groenewegen et al. (2003).

checks.claim: Makita et al. (2005) found a novel SCN5A mutation in a Japanese family with congenital atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: The novel SCN5A mutation L212P was identified in the proband (age 11 years) and his father.
checks.explanation: The novel SCN5A mutation in the family is supported, but Japanese ethnicity is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the Japanese family with congenital atrial standstill studied by Makita et al. (2005), the novel SCN5A mutation was inherited together with connexin-40 polymorphisms.
checks.evidence_quote: the proband, but not his father, carries Cx40 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother.
checks.explanation: The affected proband coinherited the SCN5A mutation and the Cx40 polymorphisms.

checks.claim: The findings of Makita et al. (2005) supported the model of SCN5A and GJA5 coinheritance in atrial standstill proposed by Groenewegen et al. (2003).
checks.evidence_quote: Incomplete penetrance observed in atrial standstill has been attributed in part to the digenic inheritance of polymorphisms in the atrial-specific gap junction connexin 40 (Cx40) in conjunction with an SCN5A mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract refers to a prior digenic model and the findings are consistent with it, but Groenewegen et al. (2003) is not named.

paragraphs.text: In a family with atrial standstill, Groenewegen et al. (2003) identified a heterozygous asp1275-to-asn (D1275N) mutation in the SCN5A gene. The mutation cosegregated with the disease together with a rare connexin-40 (GJA5) regulatory-region genotype. Functional studies showed only subtle changes in sodium channel gating.

checks.claim: Groenewegen et al. (2003) identified a heterozygous asp1275-to-asn (D1275N) mutation in the SCN5A gene in a family with atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: Candidate gene screening revealed a novel mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A (D1275N) in all three affected living relatives
checks.explanation: Heterozygosity not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the atrial standstill family studied by Groenewegen et al. (2003), the SCN5A D1275N mutation cosegregated with the disease together with a rare connexin-40 (GJA5) regulatory-region genotype.
checks.evidence_quote: The three living AS patients exclusively coinherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the SCN5A-D1275N mutation.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Groenewegen et al. (2003) showed only subtle changes in sodium channel gating with the SCN5A D1275N mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: SCN5A-D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation compared with wild-type channels.
